picks.title: A Buddhist Monk's Candid Truths About Dissatisfaction, Anger & Finding Happiness
picks.summary: In today's episode, host Rebecca Gauthier interviews Buddhist monk Gen Kelsang Dragpa.Gen Dragpa shares his journey from a discontented youth to finding deep purpose through Kadampa Buddhism. Reflecting on his personal struggles with anger, expectations, and a painful relationship separation, he explains how Buddha's teachings function as a supportive mirror - helping us understand our own minds rather than blaming external circumstances. picks.reason: Buddhist monk discusses dissatisfaction, anger, and happiness through Buddha's teachings.

picks.title: Anapanasati | Ajahn Brahm | November 2011
picks.summary:
Ajahn Brahm gives a talk on the practice of mindfulness of breathing – Anapanasati. Anapanasati is the meditation system taught by the Buddha in which mindfulness of breathing is used to develop both calm and insight. Taken from a talk given during the Nov 2011 retreat at Jhana Grove:  https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL934614E556AB3C00

picks.title: Ajahn Viradhammo: The Four Noble Truths
picks.summary:
(Tisarana Buddhist Monastery) The theme of this Sunday talk, the Four Noble truths. Buddhist traditions may vary in many ways, but the one common teaching in each one is this one. 
Is there a wellbeing that is not relative to situations? That remains unchanged. This was the Buddha's realisation. And the core of the teaching above.
It allows one to take responsibility for ones discontent.To really understand how things work.
picks.reason: A clear teaching on the Four Noble Truths, core Buddhist doctrine.

picks.title: The Wisdom of Knowing When | Bhante Joe
picks.summary: How can we know when to speak, remain silent, persevere, or change our approach? In this Dhamma talk, Bhante Joe explores the Buddhist teaching of knowing the right time and place. Drawing on his early years as a monk and the contrasting behavior of senior Thai Forest teachers, he explains how Buddhist practice unifies apparent opposites: faith and discernment, restraint and lightness, serenity and insight.
